DECIDING; TOST; the INTERVAL decides EQUIVALENT, POINT AND INTERVAL decide DIFFERENT: per corpus D_q = mean_{s=0..19} NMI_EVAL(Q8, 1024) - mean_{s=0..19} NMI_EVAL(Q4, 1024) at K_f 60/150/77; delta_c = in-run max-min over seeds 0-4 of the Q4 arm's EVAL fine NMI; SE_total = sqrt(SE_boot^2 + var_seed/20), var_seed = sample variance over 20 seeds of the per-seed Q8-Q4 difference; EQUIVALENT iff D_q +/- 1.645 SE_total inside +/-delta_c; DIFFERENT iff |D_q| > delta_c AND D_q +/- 1.96 SE_total excludes 0; NEITHER otherwise. plain_description.what: Clusters three intent datasets (MASSIVE, Banking77, CLINC) with k-means using the qwen3 embedding model at two compression levels (4-bit Q4_K_M vs 8-bit Q8_0) and checks whether cluster quality is the same within the normal seed-to-seed noise.
plain_description.why: The thesis uses a compressed embedder; if compression changed the clusters, embedder comparisons could be an artefact of compression.
plain_description.information: Equivalence clears compression as a confound; a difference would require re-running with higher precision. Result: done; equivalent within seed noise on MASSIVE and Banking77 (CLINC equivalent but descriptive only), so not a confound between these two levels. Precision above 8-bit is untested, and it does not explain why another embedder (gemma) scored higher.
